minutes.headline: School Committee approved a utility line transfer and backed a student time capsule for the new school.
minutes.summary: The meeting covered a line-item transfer from electricity to natural gas, supported by conservation savings. The superintendent reported on state testing hearings and student awards. Turkey Hill students presented a time capsule project and the committee voted support. Student council and a Latin trip were presented, and a departing member gave farewell remarks.

what_happened.line: The committee took up a line-item transfer from the electricity line to the natural gas line; a motion was made, but the result is not audible.
The business manager said conservation had left room in the electricity line, and that supply costs rose faster for electricity than for gas.
Turkey Hill students presented a time capsule project, and a motion to support it and find a place in the new building was made; the result is not audible.
The committee agreed to add a long-term capital plan as a future discussion or workshop topic.
The superintendent noted that overseas student trips cost families several thousand dollars, so early notice lets families fundraise.

why_it_matters: Utility lines are paid from the school budget, so shifts between electricity and gas show how energy prices and conservation affect what the district asks taxpayers to fund.
A long-term capital plan would shape future building and equipment requests, and could bring borrowing or spending questions to a Town Meeting vote.
